newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says ASEAN to increase growth centres.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says ASEAN to increase growth centres.

text.p: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is considering increasing the number of economic growth areas in the region, an Indonesian cabinet minister said on Wednesday.

"The ASEAN governments, including Indonesia, are determined to continue cooperating in the development of growth centres," Coordinating Minister for Distribution and Production Hartarto told participants at a seminar on regional economies.
"The countries are considering the possibility to enlarge the sub-region growth centers and are also considering the possibility to develop other growth centres," Hartarto said.
Hartarto, however, did not say where more centres were planned.
ASEAN, which consists of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Phillipines, Singapore and Vietnam, has so far developed three economic growth centres.
The first, called the Indonesia-Malaysia-Singapore Growth Triangle, includes Indonesia's Riau region, Malaysia's Johore Bahru and Singapore.
The second is the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle which joins Aceh, North and West Sumatra in Indonesia, Thailand's southern provinces and Malaysia's western states.
The Brunei-Indonesia-Malaysia-Philippines East ASEAN Growth Area is the latest.
It includes the Indonesian provinces of Central and South Kalimantan and Central, South and Southeast Sulawesi with Malaysia's Sabah state, the Philippines' southern provinces and Brunei.
